name: Jaare-oregim
overview: Jaare-oregim is a male biblical figure identified specifically as the Bethlehemite, as noted in 2 Samuel 21:19. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture provides limited additional information about his tribal affiliation or other personal details.
namesAndTitles: The name Jaare-oregim appears as a proper name in 2 Samuel 21:19 without an indicated meaning. Related names listed include Dodo, meaning 'beloved,' and Jair, meaning 'he gives light,' though these names are not directly attributed to Jaare-oregim himself.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Jaare-oregim is the son of Elhanan, as referenced in 2 Samuel 21:19. No further family relationships are recorded for him beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jaare-oregim's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his identification as a Bethlehemite and his familial link to Elhanan, situating him within the historical and genealogical context of Israel. While details about his life and deeds are scarce, his mention contributes to the record of notable individuals associated with Bethlehem during the period described in 2 Samuel.
